questions.stem: Right to Education (Article 21A) was added by which amendment?
questions.explanation: 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A: free and compulsory education for children 6-14 years. Right to Education Act, 2009 operationalised this.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which Fundamental Right was removed from the Indian Constitution by the 44th Amendment?

options.option_text: Right to Property (Article 31 — now only a legal right under Article 300A)

questions.explanation: 44th Amendment (1978) removed the Right to Property from Fundamental Rights. Article 31 deleted; Article 300A added making it a constitutional right (not fundamental).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 32 of the Indian Constitution provides for:

options.option_text: Right to Constitutional Remedies — the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights

questions.explanation: Article 32 (Dr. Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution): right to move SC for FRs enforcement via writs (habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, quo warranto).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which writ is issued when a person is detained without legal justification?
questions.explanation: Habeas Corpus: protects against arbitrary detention. Court orders authority to produce the detained person and justify the detention. Available against both state and private individuals.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 15 prohibits discrimination on which grounds?

options.option_text: Religion, race, caste, sex, and place of birth

questions.explanation: Article 15: no discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. Clauses 15(3) and 15(4) allow positive discrimination for women, children, and backward classes.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 19 guarantees six freedoms. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

options.option_text: Right to move freely throughout India

questions.explanation: Article 19 six freedoms: (a) speech and expression, (b) peaceful assembly, (c) form associations, (d) move freely, (e) reside anywhere, (g) practice any profession/trade. 'Freedom from taxation' is not included.
questions.subject: Polity

options.option_text: Abolishes untouchability and makes its practice a punishable offence

questions.explanation: Article 17: Untouchability is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden. The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 enforce this.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The right to privacy was recognised as a Fundamental Right under Article 21 by the Supreme Court in:

options.option_text: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)
Menaka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)

questions.explanation: Puttaswamy case (2017): 9-judge bench unanimously held that privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21 (right to life and personal liberty). Overruled the ADM Jabalpur (1976) judgment.
questions.subject: Polity

options.option_text: The State (as defined in Article 12) and in some cases private individuals

questions.explanation: Article 12: 'State' includes the Union, state governments, local bodies, and 'other authorities'. Courts have extended some FRs against private entities under certain circumstances.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which Article protects citizens against double jeopardy and self-incrimination?
questions.explanation: Article 20: (1) Protection against ex-post facto laws; (2) No double jeopardy (tried twice for same offence); (3) No self-incrimination (cannot be compelled to be witness against oneself).
questions.subject: Polity

options.option_text: Freedom of conscience and right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion
Right to establish religious institutions with state funding
Right to teach religion in government schools

questions.explanation: Article 25: freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practice, and propagate religion (subject to public order, morality, and health). 'Propagate' is the contentious word — some see it as permitting conversion.
